t: Inca oral history, recorded by Spanish chroniclers, says the fortress was built under Pachacuti and his successors Topa Inca Yupanqui and Huayna Capac, to serve as the head of the lion-shaped city of Cusco.

Its terrace walls use some of the largest stones in pre-Hispanic America, set without mortar; the largest limestone block is estimated at 128 tonnes to almost 200 tonnes and was moved an estimated 35 km from Rumicolca.
After the siege of Cusco the Spaniards pulled down much of the complex for building stone, so that today mostly the blocks too large to move remain.
dyk: Pedro Cieza de León wrote in 1553 that the Inca had the provinces supply 20,000 men for the work, of whom 4,000 quarried the stone and 6,000 hauled it with great cables of leather and cabuya.
ev: The earliest occupation of the hilltop, as indicated by surface collections of pottery
The Imperial Inca expanded the settlement with dry stone walls of huge stones
Pedro Cieza de León wrote his account of the fortress and of its pillaging by the Spaniards
Garcilaso de la Vega described how the Spaniards pulled down the smooth masonry for their houses
Cusco and Sacsayhuamán together were placed on the UNESCO World Heritage List
Archaeologists found further ruins at the periphery of the site

f.made: Built by the Inca; Inca oral history, as the Spanish chroniclers recorded it, places the work in the reigns of Pachacuti, Topa Inca Yupanqui and Huayna Capac, with labour supplied by the provinces
f.form: A fortified ceremonial complex on a steep hill at 3,701 metres, with a great plaza and three massive terrace walls of dry stone, the longest about 400 metres long and about 6 metres tall
f.where: On the northern outskirts of Cusco, Peru, the historic capital of the Inca Empire
f.known: walls of huge limestone blocks cut to fit without mortar; the great plaza; the lion-shaped plan of Cusco, with the fortress as its head; the Spanish quarrying of the site; the festivals of Inti Raymi and Warachikuy held there
